newsitem.title: INDIA: Reliance helps push up Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Reliance helps push up Delhi shares.

text.p: Strong buying by foreign institutional investors in Reliance Industries on Thursday helped to push share prices to a higher close on the Delhi Stock Exchange, brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index finished a roller-coaster day up 3.16 points at 861.11 points.
Traders said news that the board of directors of Reliance will meet on June 26 to discuss a bonus issue triggered buying.
"Large-scale speculative activity in Reliance Industries mainly enthused the sentiment," said Vikas Sharma of brokers Multiple Investments.
"The firm will be meeting for a bonus on June 26," a Reliance spokesman told Reuters in Bombay on Thursday.
Reliance surged 21.45 rupees, or 6.7 percent, to 341.50 after the company announcement.
Reliance has announced two bonus share issues since it was listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on January 23, 1978.
Both times the firm gave investors three bonus shares for every five held, and early speculation in the stock markets was that the company was likely to maintain this ratio.
State Bank of India (SBI) bucked the trend to close 0.90 rupee lower at 323.60 on profit-taking by speculators, brokers said.

SBI announced on Thursday that net profit rose to 13.29 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) from 8.32 billion, while earnings per share increased to 26.66 rupees from 17.54. The bank raised its dividend to 4.00 rupees from 3.50.
